tests.name: Hypothesis testing and p-values
tests.summary: What a null hypothesis, test statistic, and p-value really are, and what they are not.

tests.name: Confidence intervals
tests.summary: How to read a 95% CI, why it beats a p-value alone, and how sample size changes it.

tests.name: Type I and II errors, and power
tests.summary: False positives, false negatives, power, and why multiple testing inflates errors.

tests.name: Effect sizes and clinical significance
tests.summary: Statistical vs clinical significance: mean differences, Cohen's d, and the MCID.

tests.name: Sample size & power: means and proportions
tests.summary: How many patients per arm to detect a difference in means or response rates.

tests.name: Sample size for time-to-event studies
tests.summary: Number of events and patients needed to detect a hazard ratio (Schoenfeld).

tests.name: Shapiro–Wilk test
tests.summary: Tests whether a sample plausibly comes from a normal distribution.

tests.name: Levene's test
tests.summary: Tests whether groups have equal variances.

tests.name: One-sample t-test
tests.summary: Compares a sample mean to a known reference value.

tests.name: One-sample z-test
tests.summary: Compares a sample mean to a reference value when the population SD is truly known (rare in practice).

tests.name: Independent two-sample t-test (Student & Welch)
tests.summary: Compares means of two independent groups, such as treatment vs placebo.

tests.name: Paired t-test
tests.summary: Compares two measurements on the same subjects, such as before vs after treatment.

tests.name: One-way ANOVA
tests.summary: Compares means across three or more independent groups.

tests.name: Welch's ANOVA
tests.summary: Compares means of three or more groups without assuming equal variances.

tests.name: Repeated-measures ANOVA
tests.summary: Compares means across three or more time points on the same subjects.

tests.name: Two-way (factorial) ANOVA
tests.summary: Tests two factors and their interaction, such as drug × sex.

tests.name: MANOVA
tests.summary: Compares groups on several continuous outcomes at once.

tests.name: ANCOVA
tests.summary: Compares group means adjusting for a baseline covariate; the standard RCT analysis of change.

tests.name: Tukey's HSD
tests.summary: All pairwise comparisons after ANOVA with family-wise error control.

tests.name: Dunnett's test
tests.summary: Compares several treatment arms to a single control arm.

tests.name: Multiple-comparison corrections (Bonferroni, Holm, BH)
tests.summary: Adjusts p-values when you run many tests or endpoints.

tests.name: Wilcoxon signed-rank test
tests.summary: Nonparametric alternative to the paired t-test.

tests.name: Mann–Whitney U (Wilcoxon rank-sum) test
tests.summary: Nonparametric alternative to the independent t-test.

tests.name: Kruskal–Wallis test
tests.summary: Nonparametric alternative to one-way ANOVA.

tests.name: Friedman test
tests.summary: Nonparametric alternative to repeated-measures ANOVA.

tests.name: Sign test
tests.summary: The simplest paired test: counts how many differences are positive vs negative.

tests.name: One-sample proportion (exact binomial) test
tests.summary: Compares an observed response rate to a target rate.

tests.name: Two-proportion z-test
tests.summary: Compares response rates between two independent groups.

tests.name: Chi-square test of independence
tests.summary: Tests association between two categorical variables in an r × c table.

tests.name: Chi-square goodness-of-fit test
tests.summary: Compares observed category counts to expected proportions.

tests.name: Fisher's exact test
tests.summary: Exact test for 2 × 2 tables, especially with small expected counts.

tests.name: McNemar's test
tests.summary: Compares paired binary outcomes, such as the same patients before and after.

tests.name: Cochran–Mantel–Haenszel test
tests.summary: Tests a treatment–outcome association across strata, such as study sites.

tests.name: Risk difference, relative risk, odds ratio, and NNT
tests.summary: The effect measures clinicians report for binary outcomes, with confidence intervals.

tests.name: Tests for trend (Cochran–Armitage, Jonckheere–Terpstra)
tests.summary: Tests a dose–response pattern across ordered groups.

tests.name: Cochran's Q test
tests.summary: Compares a binary outcome across three or more conditions on the same subjects.

tests.name: Pearson correlation
tests.summary: Measures linear association between two continuous variables.

tests.name: Spearman rank correlation
tests.summary: Measures monotonic association using ranks.

tests.name: Kendall's tau
tests.summary: A rank correlation that handles ties and small samples well.

tests.name: Linear regression
tests.summary: Models a continuous outcome from one or more predictors.

tests.name: Logistic regression
tests.summary: Models a binary outcome and reports adjusted odds ratios.

tests.name: Ordinal logistic (proportional odds) regression
tests.summary: Models an ordered outcome such as the modified Rankin Scale with a common odds ratio.

tests.name: Multinomial logistic regression
tests.summary: Models an unordered categorical outcome with three or more levels.

tests.name: Conditional logistic regression
tests.summary: The analysis for matched case–control studies.

tests.name: Firth (penalized) logistic regression
tests.summary: Logistic regression that still works with rare events, small samples, or separation.

tests.name: Poisson & negative binomial regression
tests.summary: Models counts or event rates, such as exacerbations per patient-year.

tests.name: Linear mixed-effects models (MMRM)
tests.summary: Longitudinal or clustered data with missing visits; the workhorse of modern trials.

tests.name: Generalized estimating equations (GEE)
tests.summary: Population-averaged effects for correlated binary or count outcomes.

tests.name: Kaplan–Meier estimator
tests.summary: Estimates survival curves and median survival with censoring.

tests.name: Log-rank test
tests.summary: Compares survival curves between groups.

tests.name: Cox proportional hazards regression
tests.summary: Estimates adjusted hazard ratios for time-to-event outcomes.

tests.name: Competing risks (cumulative incidence & Fine–Gray)
tests.summary: Time-to-event analysis when another event, such as death, prevents the event of interest.

tests.name: Cohen's kappa
tests.summary: Agreement between two raters on a categorical rating, beyond chance.

tests.name: Intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC)
tests.summary: Reliability of continuous measurements across raters or repeats.

tests.name: Cronbach's alpha
tests.summary: Internal consistency of a multi-item questionnaire or scale.

tests.name: Bland–Altman analysis
tests.summary: Agreement between two measurement methods: bias and limits of agreement.

tests.name: ROC curve, AUC, sensitivity & specificity
tests.summary: Evaluates how well a score or biomarker discriminates disease status.

tests.name: Equivalence (TOST) & non-inferiority tests
tests.summary: Shows two treatments differ by less than a pre-specified margin.

tests.name: Meta-analysis (fixed and random effects)
tests.summary: Pools results across studies, with heterogeneity and forest plots.

tests.name: Missing data and multiple imputation
tests.summary: Why complete-case analysis can mislead, and how multiple imputation works.

tests.name: Propensity scores
tests.summary: Adjusting for confounding in observational studies by matching or weighting.

tests.name: Bootstrap and permutation tests
tests.summary: Assumption-light inference by resampling your own data.
